title: Complete Erdős Problem #104: Unit Circles Through Three Points (Work in Progress)

problemStatement.formal: n \text{ points in } \mathbb{R}^2 \implies \#\{\text{unit circles containing} \ge 3 \text{ points}\} = O(n^{3/2})
problemStatement.plain: Given n points in ℝ², how many unit circles contain at least 3 points? Known: Ω(n^{3/2}) ≤ answer ≤ O(n²). Conjecture: O(n^{3/2}). OPEN ($100 prize).
whyMatters: A \$100 Erdős prize problem tightening incidence bounds between $\Omega(n^{3/2})$ and $O(n^2)$.
